en.title: Public holidays
en.summary: Main holidays and how to wish people well on them.

paragraphs: Two friends talk about Christmas plans.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: What are you doing for Christmas?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I am going to visit my family. We always eat turkey on Christmas Day.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: That sounds lovely. Do you open presents in the morning?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes, the children wake up very early!

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Well, Merry Christmas to you all.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: And a happy New Year to you!

paragraphs: **1. The present continuous can express plans.** With a time word it describes a fixed arrangement: I am visiting my family on Christmas Day. See Introduction to Grammar: Future and other tenses.

paragraphs: **2. Wishes use a fixed phrase.** Say Happy + holiday or Merry Christmas. The reply is often You too or The same to you. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

items: In the United Kingdom a public holiday is also called a **bank holiday**.
Major holidays include Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year and Easter.
In the United States Thanksgiving and the Fourth of July are national holidays.

paragraphs: Many British families eat a Christmas dinner together on 25 December. The day after is Boxing Day, a time for visiting relatives or shopping in the sales.
